response: There is still no dedicated solar and stellar astrophysics cluster — papers on stellar evolution, stellar atmospheres, solar physics, and related topics must be consolidated into one. The "Exoplanet Formation and Characterization" cluster remains a catch-all mixing neutron star measurements, planetary nebulae, and solar system bodies with actual exoplanet science; neutron star papers belong in high-energy astrophysics and solar system/icy moon papers in planetary astrophysics. The "Black Holes and Galaxies" cluster should be split into a clean galactic/extragalactic cluster (galaxies, ISM, stellar populations) and a high-energy cluster (black holes, AGN, supernovae, compact objects), rather than lumping them together. The goal remains exactly six clusters matching the six defined subject areas, with no miscellaneous bins.
